1.name: Gear case
1.note: The cast housing for the drive shaft and the bevel pair. It holds the spindle upright under the governor.

2.name: Drive shaft
2.note: Brings engine speed in from the belt pulley and carries it to the bevel gears.

3.name: Bevel wheel
3.note: The larger of the bevel pair. It turns the drive through 90° and steps the speed to the spindle at 1.5 times engine speed.

4.name: Bevel pinion
4.note: Meshes with the wheel to turn the spindle. Its ratio is why the spindle runs faster than the engine.

5.name: Bush
5.note: Bronze sleeves that carry the shafts in the gear case.

6.name: Flat-belt pulley
6.note: Takes the drive from the engine by belt. This is where engine speed enters the governor.

7.name: Parallel key
7.note: Locks the pulley, the wheel and the pinion to their shafts so they turn together.

8.name: Spindle
8.note: The vertical shaft that spins the whole governor. The sleeve slides up and down on it.

9.name: Stop collar
9.note: Limits the sleeve's travel at the top and bottom of its range.

10.name: Head
10.note: The block at the top of the spindle. The upper arms pivot on it.

11.name: Hex nut
11.note: Holds the head on the end of the spindle.

12.name: Upper arm
12.note: Hangs each ball from the head. As the ball swings outward the arm's angle sets the sleeve's height.

13.name: Flyball
13.note: The sensor. Faster spin throws the balls outward and lifts the sleeve, so speed becomes height.

14.name: Lower link
14.note: Joins each ball to the sleeve, so the balls lift the sleeve as they rise.

15.name: Pin
15.note: Pivots for the arm, link and sleeve joints.

16.name: Sleeve (load)
16.note: The weight that makes this a Porter governor. It adds to the pull that holds the balls in, so the speed has to rise further to lift it.

17.name: Swivel collar, split
17.note: Lets the bell crank's fork hold the sleeve while the sleeve spins. It carries only the sleeve's lift to the crank.

18.name: Bell crank
18.note: A lever that turns the sleeve's vertical lift into the valve link's pull. This is the controller's output.

19.name: Valve link
19.note: Connects the bell crank to the valve stem.

20.name: Valve stem
20.note: Moves the valve up or down inside its gland.

21.name: Double-beat valve
21.note: Two discs on one stem. Steam pushes them in opposite directions, so a light governor can move it. Full lift shuts it.

22.name: Seat ring
22.note: The two seats the valve discs close on.

23.name: Valve body
23.note: The steam passage. The valve sits across it and the opening sets how much steam reaches the engine.

24.name: Bonnet with fulcrum post
24.note: Closes the valve body and carries the bell crank's pivot.

25.name: Gland
25.note: Presses the packing against the stem so steam does not leak out where the stem passes through.

26.name: Packing ring
26.note: The seal between stem and bonnet.

27.name: Stud + nut
27.note: Clamps the bonnet to the valve body.

28.name: Hex nut
28.note: Locks the valve disc to its stem.
